correctness.rationale: For a source incidence (i,S), eliminating block potentials leaves the scalar lambda*v/k on mean-zero point potentials. This gives x_i=(k-1)/(lambda*v), x_j=-1/(lambda*v) on S minus i, and zero elsewhere; each block potential is its average x minus 1/k on S alone. Thus the block S contributes 1, since lambda*v>k. On every other block T through i only the edge from i is positive, with absolute block sum 2[(k-1)^2+b_T]/(k*lambda*v); on a block missing i the negative and positive parts are separated by membership in S, giving 2b_T(k-b_T)/(k*lambda*v), including the zero cases. Here b_T=|T intersect (S minus i)|. The sums of b_T on the first class and b_T(k-b_T) on the second are (k-1)(lambda-1) and (k-1)(v-k)(lambda-tau) respectively. The latter count excludes exactly tau blocks through i for each cross pair. Substitution of (k-1)r=lambda(v-1) gives the claimed Q formula for every column. Q_ee=1/k+(k-1)/(lambda*v) is strictly between 0 and 1, so replacing Q by I-Q adds 1-2Q_ee to each absolute column sum. Symmetry gives the same infinity norms. The inverse-incidence and Steiner quadruple simplifications agree (e.g. Q=11/4 and P=3 at v=8,k=4,tau=1); no transitivity is used.
residual_risks: The reported 1,096 finite columns and 116 grounded-Laplacian columns are corroboration; the listed instances do not by themselves test asymmetric designs or general k.
No inference about arbitrary weights, strength two, or nonorthogonal norm minimizers is made.

evidence: The transfer-current theorems provide general upper bounds rather than equality.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The symmetric-design hypothesis does not cover the target: if the underlying 2-design were symmetric, then r=k, but the design derived at any point is a nontrivial 2-design on v-1 points with r blocks and requires r>=v-1 by its full-rank point Gram matrix (lambda>tau). This contradicts k<=v-2.

evidence: The prior current framework gives a linear solution but not sums of absolute values.
The decisive b_T(k-b_T) sum measures pair incidence while excluding one point; its lambda-tau factor needs triple balance or an equivalent additional hypothesis.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither exact pair-unique or symmetric-family solutions, nor asymptotic localization bounds for all graphs, supply this count or equality on the target regime.
searches: General transfer-current theorems at arXiv:1708.01632 and arXiv:2605.24130

evidence: The canonical cut projection is the electrical transfer-current operator; its column norm is the absolute current emanating from a unit transfer along one incidence.
Resultary 431fab1ed962 and 2c1550cf6033 prove exact electrical/projector results for Steiner 2-designs with pair multiplicity one.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The electrical restatement does not make the evaluation automatic, and lambda>1 in the stated 3-design range. In particular a Steiner quadruple system here has triple index one, not pair index one.
searches: Resultary: endpoint Hodge norms, design incidence graphs, electrical bypasses and transfer currents

evidence: Exact current-class tables exist for pair-unique or symmetric incidence designs.
Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii gives (n+1)/2 for a cut projection on the n-cube.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are genuine exact-computation precedents, but not a table of the claimed 3-design norms; the proof for the indexed graph families cannot be substituted for all simple 3-designs.

originality.rationale: The exact norms for general strength-three incidence graphs, determined by third-order overlap rather than a symmetry hypothesis, pass the scoped comparison. Electrical-current representations, weaker universal bounds, and exact norms for other graph families or design regimes are prior work, not contributions of this record.
residual_risks: Indexed and accessible passages do not establish priority. Older exact incidence-network calculations may use other terminology; some broader search results were uninformative or unavailable in the completed lookup.

value.rationale: Exact endpoint norms are natural measures of worst-case absolute electrical transfer and of the canonical cycle projection. A formula for every edge across a family defined by incidence balance rather than group symmetry is informative beyond general bounds. In particular designs with the same (v,k) can have different constants, quantified by the inverse pair-incidence dependence; the strength-three calculation explains the difference and provides exact benchmarks.
residual_risks: An exact canonical norm does not assert that the canonical complement is optimal among nonorthogonal projections.
